subject: Physics
plain_formula: dθ = ds / r (rad), dΩ = dA / r² (sr)
ncert_core_rule: 7 fundamental SI base quantities define all physical measurement. Radian and steradian are supplementary dimensionless units.
author_book_nuance: H.C. Verma: A quantity can possess units without dimensions (rad, sr), but no quantity can possess dimensions without units.
neet_trap_point: Students assume all quantities with units have dimensions. Plane angle has unit radian but dimension [M^0 L^0 T^0].
chapter_core_topics: Units, SI Units, Errors, Dimensions & Applications

subject: Physics
next_video_title: Dimensions of Physical Quantities & Common Equivalences
ncert_core_rule: Derived units are algebraic combinations of base units. SI prefixes represent powers of 10 from 10^-15 to 10^12.
author_book_nuance: D.C. Pandey: Double prefixes are strictly forbidden in SI rules (e.g., write pF, never μμF).
neet_trap_point: Attaching prefixes to kilogram instead of gram. Since kg already has 'kilo', write 1 mg for 10^-6 kg, not 1 μkg.
chapter_core_topics: Units, SI Units, Errors, Dimensions & Applications

subject: Physics
concept_title: Dimensions of Physical Quantities & Common Equivalences
ncert_core_rule: Dimensions of a physical quantity are powers to which base units are raised to represent that quantity.
author_book_nuance: Halliday & Resnick: Torque and Work share identical dimensions [M L^2 T^-2] but are fundamentally different: Torque is a vector, Work is a scalar.
neet_trap_point: Confusing quantities that share identical dimensions with being physically identical. Never equate their physical nature.
chapter_core_topics: Units, SI Units, Errors, Dimensions & Applications

subject: Physics
next_video_title: Classification of Errors & Mean Absolute Error
ncert_core_rule: Physical quantities having identical dimensions alone can be added, subtracted, or equated. Arguments of trig, exp, and log functions must be dimensionless.
author_book_nuance: I.E. Irodov: In (P + a/V^2)(V - b) = RT, dimensional homogeneity dictates [a/V^2] = [P] and [b] = [V].
neet_trap_point: Assuming dimensional consistency guarantees physical correctness. Pure numbers (like 1/2 or 2π) cannot be derived or checked by dimensional analysis.
chapter_core_topics: Units, SI Units, Errors, Dimensions & Applications

subject: Physics
concept_title: Classification of Errors & Mean Absolute Error
plain_formula: a_mean = (Σ a_i) / n, Δa_mean = (Σ |a_mean - a_i|) / n
ncert_core_rule: Systematic errors are unidirectional and eliminated by calibration. Random errors fluctuate and are minimized by taking the arithmetic mean of repeated readings.
author_book_nuance: H.C. Verma: Absolute error is always positive. The sum of signed deviations from the mean is always identically zero.
neet_trap_point: Taking the algebraic sum of deviations instead of the magnitude |Δa_i|, which falsely gives zero mean error.
chapter_core_topics: Units, SI Units, Errors, Dimensions & Applications

subject: Physics
next_video_title: Measuring Instruments: Vernier Callipers & Screw Gauge
latex_formula: Z = \frac{A^p B^q}{C^r} \implies \frac{\Delta Z}{Z} = p\frac{\Delta A}{A} + q\frac{\Delta B}{B} + r\frac{\Delta C}{C}
plain_formula: Z = (A^p * B^q) / C^r  ==>  ΔZ/Z = p*(ΔA/A) + q*(ΔB/B) + r*(ΔC/C)
ncert_core_rule: In worst-case error estimation, fractional errors for product, quotient, and power relations always add with their positive power coefficients.
author_book_nuance: D.C. Pandey: Even if C is in the denominator (C^r), its fractional error is added with coefficient +r, never subtracted!
neet_trap_point: Subtracting errors for quantities in the denominator. Errors always accumulate in maximum uncertainty analysis.
chapter_core_topics: Units, SI Units, Errors, Dimensions & Applications

subject: Physics
concept_title: Measuring Instruments: Vernier Callipers & Screw Gauge
plain_formula: LC = Pitch / Circular Divisions, True = Observed - (±Zero Error)
ncert_citation: NCERT Class 11 Part 1, Chapter 2 Appendix & Practical Manual
ncert_core_rule: Vernier LC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD. Screw gauge LC = Pitch / Total circular divisions. True reading = Observed reading - (Zero Error).
author_book_nuance: NCERT Lab Manual: Positive zero error is SUBTRACTED; negative zero error is ADDED (- (-e) = +e).
neet_trap_point: Inverting zero error signs: Positive zero error (+e) must be subtracted, while negative zero error (-e) must be added.
chapter_core_topics: Units, SI Units, Errors, Dimensions & Applications

subject: Physics
next_video_title: Chapter 1 Complete • Ready for Unit 2: Kinematics
latex_formula: \text{Add/Sub: Least Decimal Places}, \quad \text{Mul/Div: Least Significant Figures}
plain_formula: Add/Sub: Retain least decimal places | Mul/Div: Retain least significant figures
ncert_core_rule: Significant figures reflect measurement precision. Leading zeros are never significant; trailing zeros with a decimal point are significant.
author_book_nuance: H.C. Verma: In addition 100.1 + 0.003 = 100.103 -> 100.1 (1 decimal place). Do not count total significant figures in addition/subtraction.
neet_trap_point: Applying the multiplication rule (least sig figs) to addition/subtraction, which is governed strictly by the least decimal places.
chapter_core_topics: Units, SI Units, Errors, Dimensions & Applications

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Slope of the position-time curve represents instantaneous velocity.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Negative slope indicates velocity in opposite direction, not necessarily deceleration.
neet_trap_point: Confusing slope of x-t graph (velocity) with slope of v-t graph (acceleration).
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Any 2D vector can be resolved into two mutually perpendicular orthogonal components.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 2: Components of a vector behave independently along x and y coordinates.
neet_trap_point: Assigning cosine to vertical axis when angle was given with horizontal.
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Time of flight is determined purely by the vertical component of initial velocity.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: The horizontal velocity component vx has zero acceleration and does not affect the time spent in the air.
neet_trap_point: Question specifies angle with vertical axis instead of horizontal (swapping sin with cos).
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: At maximum height, the vertical component of velocity is zero while horizontal velocity remains v0*cos(theta).
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Speed at the top is not zero; it equals v0*cos(theta). Kinetic energy is minimum but non-zero.
neet_trap_point: Confusing total velocity being zero with only vertical velocity component being zero at top of trajectory.
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Horizontal range is identical for complementary projection angles theta and (90 - theta) at the same initial speed.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Although ranges are equal for theta and 90-theta, maximum heights and times of flight are strictly unequal.
neet_trap_point: Assuming time of flight and maximum height are also equal when ranges are equal for complementary angles.
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
plain_formula: y = x · tan(θ) - (g · x²) / (2 · v₀² · cos²(θ))
ncert_core_rule: The trajectory of a projectile is parabolic in nature, relating vertical coordinate y to horizontal coordinate x.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Alternative formulation y = x*tan(theta)*(1 - x/R) simplifies range-based NEET problems instantly.
neet_trap_point: Confusing tan(theta) factor with cot(theta) when comparing experimental trajectory equations.
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Acceleration in uniform circular motion always points radially inward toward the center of the circle.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 7: Speed is constant but velocity continuously changes direction; therefore acceleration is non-zero and perpendicular to velocity.
neet_trap_point: Assuming acceleration is zero because speed is constant in uniform circular motion.
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Area under velocity-time graph equals displacement; slope equals acceleration.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Negative area represents negative displacement, not distance traveled.
neet_trap_point: Calculating distance instead of displacement by ignoring sign of negative area!
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Relative velocity of object A with respect to B is vector difference v_A - v_B.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Shortest time to cross river requires heading directly perpendicular to flow.
neet_trap_point: Confusing shortest path with shortest time in river-boat problems!
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
plain_formula: t = sqrt(2h / g), R = v₀ · sqrt(2h / g)
ncert_core_rule: Vertical motion is identical to free fall from height h; initial vertical velocity is zero.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Horizontal speed v0 has zero effect on the time taken to hit the ground.
neet_trap_point: Believing a faster launched projectile takes longer to hit the ground than one dropped!
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Resolve g into components parallel (g sin beta) and perpendicular (g cos beta) to incline.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Treat incline as new x-axis with effective gravity components.
neet_trap_point: Forgetting that acceleration along incline is non-zero (g sin beta)!
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Radius of curvature equals speed squared divided by normal acceleration component.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: At apex, total speed is vx = v0 cos theta and gravity g is purely normal.
neet_trap_point: Using total launch speed v0 instead of horizontal velocity v0 cos theta at the apex!
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Linear speed is directly proportional to radius r for particles on a rotating rigid body.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 7: All points on a rotating wheel have the same omega but different linear speeds v.
neet_trap_point: Thinking points closer to center move with higher linear velocity than the outer rim!
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion

subject: Physics
ncert_core_rule: Total acceleration has two orthogonal components: radial (centripetal) and tangential.
author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 7: Tangential acceleration changes speed; centripetal acceleration changes direction.
neet_trap_point: Forgetting tangential acceleration when speed is increasing in circular motion!
chapter_core_topics: Frame of Reference, Graphs, Vectors, Projectile, Circular Motion
